James, 1954; Parke-Bernet Galleries, Inc., New York, NY, sale no. 1615, lot no. 19, 19 October 1955; The artist, 1955; (The Downtown Gallery, New York, NY); Private collection, Toronto, Canada, 1959; (Glass Art Gallery, date unknown); Christie's, New York, NY, sale no. 6838, lot no. 388, 25 May 1989; Gerald Peters Gallery, Santa Fe, New Mexico, and Montgomery Gallery, San Francisco, California, 1989; Montgomery Gallery, San Francisco, California, 1991; (Irene Drori, Inc., Fine Art, Los Angeles, California) (Source: Lynes, 1999)
remarks_1999: Whitney Archive indicates, "Exam. at Amer. Place, March 1946. . . . No signature" [notes inscription, but identifies as by O'Keeffe]. Whitney Archive, Abiquiú Notebooks indicate, "Note: Miss O'Keeffe says this is a mate to Mrs. Dewald's "Abstraction," which was in the above exhibition [1929 An American Place] and signed and dated 1929." Abiquiú Notebooks indicates, "Note: Sold to Oliver James and purchased by O'Keeffe in 1955." (Source: Lynes, 1999)

description: A black rectangle fills the left third of the image. Two overlapping rectangles peek out from behind it. A plain black rectangle spans much of the righthand side of the composition. Behind these elements is a burgundy background.
